title: Willie Lynch's band, the Cotton Club and Edgar Hayes's 'Stardust'
summary: Mills had Lynch form a substitute band to replace Cab Calloway at the Cotton Club, with Edgar Hayes's 'Stardust' solos a hit at the Lafayette, and Lynch took Holmes back.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: You mentioned that you were in and out of Russell's band, and at one point you went into the Savoy with Willie Lynch.

Well, Willie Lynch was a drummer that Irving Mills knew, and Irving Mills was trying to get a substitute band for Cab Calloway in the Cotton Club -- to put in the Cotton Club. So Willie Lynch got a band together and was trying it out at the Savoy Ballroom. Well, we worked the Savoy for about three months, and then Mills put the band into the Cotton Club behind Cab Calloway. He was taking Cab out, he sent him on the road... And this band goes into the Cotton Club.
Well, in the meantime, I wasn't with the band when they went in the Cotton Club. But I had been back with Russell's band again, and consequently, I left them one more time -- Russell's band.
Well, can you mention that at this point Lynch's band had gone to the Lafayette Theatre and had a big success there.

Well, that was Willie's band. Well, they was... They didn't have a name then. It was just Willie Lynch and the band. So they were playing the number 'Stardust,' and they were featuring the pianist, Edgar Hayes -- he did the solos on the number 'Stardust.' And it was really a wonderful thing he did. He did wonderful solos on
it. And he was a big attraction. He was a big attraction on... What's his name?
You said they had a big production number.

A big attraction, and they had a big display where the stars were falling, and one thing and another. It was a beautiful thing to see. And they really made a big name then. So consequently, that helped Willie to get in the Cotton Club with the band quicker than if he had just been out there on his own -- one of them things.

So Mills put him in, and put Cab out on the road, and consequently, he started to change his men in the band. And Willie wanted me back in the band. Willie and I, I was just like one of his boys. It didn't make sense for me to be walking the street, and he had a job, and he could use me. So he put me back in his band. That was all right with me.
